spec.name: Blend v15
spec.notes: Multi-factor score: momentum, drift and low risk.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 1.7, annual return 9%, maximum drawdown 13%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.73 to 1.71 (change -0.01).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 1.73 to 1.73. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 1.73 (as submitted, 10 bps: 1.73); it breaks even at above 200 bps with daily turnover 0.02.
On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is 3.55 against 1.73 in research, a gap of -1.82.
The best year gives 31% of total P&L (year 7) and calm regimes give 195%; Sharpe is 5.37 in calm and -4.73 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 2 distinct specs; the best of 2 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.02, so the claimed 1.70 becomes 1.68 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.

verdict.opinion: The holdout test (EX-4) reveals a significant performance gap between the research period and the sealed period, suggesting potential overfitting or a lucky period. While other tests are supportive, the substantial difference in Sharpe ratios warrants caution. Therefore, the strategy will be restricted to paper trading to further evaluate its robustness before deploying real capital.
